data.text/markdown:
E0b. How many beats until the forces repeat?

Question

E0 showed that the second beat of every corpus run differs from the first by up to a fifth of peak. Does the flow settle if the run continues, and how far is the beat the surrogate trains on (beat 2) from the settled waveform?

Method

One coarse-grid run of the centre config s45_f100_p45, continued from 2 to 6 wingbeats (12,000 steps) on the local RTX A5000, in the corpus's own container image (pinned by digest). The deck is the committed coarse deck with only max_step, stop_time, checkpointing and the GPU memory arena changed. Coefficients come from the repo's own extractor. Each beat is resampled to a 256-point phase grid and compared with the beat before it and with beat 6; differences are RMS over the beat divided by beat 6's peak, with phase below 0.05 excluded as in E0. Control. The first 4,000 steps (the two beats the corpus has) were compared row by row with the committed coarse dataset at 80d653a. Fx, Fz, Mx and Mz are identical; the largest raw difference in any component is 2.8e-14 (Fy, My). The local run is a continuation of the corpus run, not a different one. Data used: experiments/e0b_long_run/run_s45_f100_p45/IB_Particle_1.csv (generated here, not committed) and examples/prelim_sweep/dataset.parquet at 80d653a for the control.

Result

The forces do settle, and beat 2 is most of the way there.
  • Beat 2 differs from beat 6 by 0.8% to 2.9% of peak, depending on the component (largest: CF_z). Beat 1 differs by up to 22%.
  • After beat 2 the beat-to-beat change shrinks by a factor of about 1.5 to 3.5 per beat: for CF_z it is 1.9%, 1.1%, 0.38%, 0.11% for beats 3 to 6. By beat 6 every component changes by under 0.23% of peak per beat.
  • The mean of CF_z goes 0.671 → 0.501 → 0.476 (beats 1, 2, 6): the large drop is in the first beat, and the later drift is small.
  • Running 4 beats instead of 2 would bring every component within 0.5% of peak of beat 6.
The Track B surrogate's held-out error on the fine grid is 1.1–1.8% of peak (E1; median over configs, 2.5% worst). On this config the beat-2 start-up residue (0.8%–2.9%) is the same size or larger for CF_z, CF_mx and CF_my. So the surrogate reproduces its training data more closely than that data represents steady flapping.

data.text/markdown:
Caveats

  • Coarse grid only. For this config the fine grid's beat-1-to-beat-2 change in CF_z (E0: 15% of peak) is of the same order as the coarse one here (21%), but whether the fine grid settles at the same rate was not run; a 6-beat fine run was outside this exploration's local-GPU budget.
  • One config, the centre of the sweep. E0 found the beat-1-to-beat-2 change is largest at 30° pitch, so the low-pitch configs probably settle more slowly than this one.
  • Beat 6 is the reference, not the limit. It is still moving by up to 0.23% of peak per beat, so the distances "vs last" slightly understate the distance to the truly periodic state. At the observed decay rate the remainder is about the size of that last step.
  • This experiment does not say why the flow takes several beats to settle (wake build-up, or the wing meeting its own wake through the spanwise-periodic boundary). Whatever the cause, it is a property of the corpus setup and is the same in every corpus run.

Next step

If the corpus is regenerated for any reason, run 4 beats and train on the fourth: it doubles the cost per config and cuts the start-up residue from 2.9% to 0.5% of peak on this config. Before committing to that, repeat this run for one 30°-pitch config (about 7 hours on the coarse grid on this GPU) to see the slowest case. This would also remove the kink at the beat boundary that E2 traced to non-periodic training data.
